annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "night" on page 514 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. During this Age of Men phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Freud, Sigmund. The Interpretation of Dreams. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/4349
Troy, Mark L. Mummeries of Resurrection. http://www.rosenlake.net

annotations.annotation_text: Dublin landmark "Howth" on page 514 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): grounding the cosmic dream in physical Dublin during the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. Joyce transforms this real location into a universal archetypal site — simultaneously Eden, Waterloo, Calvary, and the Elysian Fields — within the Age of Men phase.
sources: Joyce, P.W. The Origin and History of Irish Names of Places. https://archive.org/details/originandhistory01joycuoft
Mink, Louis O. A Finnegans Wake Gazetteer. https://archive.org/details/finneganswakegaz0000mink
